motivation: The first ten external tasks revealed frequent ties for the winning integer ballot. Make one change to that policy: break ties on its original minimum approval count by the unresampled empty-restoration continuous slack, then the original Gain priority. This strictly preserves every original comparison with unequal vote counts. The extra signal is computable for retained candidates using the same fitted model and ranking rows.
cohorts: Retrospective on the ten-task panel. Independently freeze this refinement before the new six-task higher-dimensional panel is scored, using the exact same feasible folds, half-width candidate slates, 100-round learner, voting rules and guards. Never use outcomes to choose a tie rule or cherry-pick datasets. Cohorts remain separate.
decision: Choose the lexicographic maximum of (minimum approval count over all restorations, original-panel empty-context slack). Identical pairs keep the first candidate in original Gain-priority order. With no strict deletion retain the anchor. Compare to discrete voting with Gain ties and point slack alone. Report U (primary descriptive), breaches, accuracy and AUC, changed nominations/finals, ties, and task-weighted paired intervals. New method must beat cheap point to justify voting, with the same 0.05 U material benefit and nonpositive breach increase as the wide protocol.
implementation: Rank in decreasing point slack, ties in Gain order. Once a completed candidate has minimum approval count b, stop examining a later candidate at its first context with count at most b. If b=4 skip remaining candidates. The first panel in the empty context and the other ballot panels can share predictions. Verify choices against complete score tables. Measure unique predicted masks, time and final guarded outcomes. The optimization is exact for this lexicographic rule and does not change the original discrete ballots.
